attempts.summary: Configured a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (AlmaLinux 9): SSH open to all, TCP/9000 accepted only from node2 (10.100.100.11) via a high-priority rich rule, and TCP/9000 rejected from everyone else (including node3) via a lower-priority generic reject rule. Fixed an initial ordering bug where firewalld's default deny-before-allow chain evaluation would have blocked node2 too, by assigning explicit rich-rule priorities (-100 accept, 100 reject) so the node2 accept rule is placed in the pre-chain evaluated before the generic reject in the post-chain. Verified live behavior with an actual TCP listener on port 9000: node2 gets HTTP 200, node3 gets connection refused, SSH from both reaches the auth stage. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3: captured boot_id/uptime baselines, triggered systemctl reboot via a detached background command so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until each node was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to a few seconds, and re-verified firewalld state/rules and actual allow/reject connectivity behavior after each node's restart.
